requirements: First coordinate shared-pool headroom; avoid migration while pool remains under emergency pressure.
Recheck activity, scheduled loads and model download locks immediately before cutover.
Copy first to an Eden-specific destination; retain internal snapshot-to-blob symlinks and any hard links; no cross-filesystem hard-link dedup assumptions.
HF hub has 51 internal symlinks and no external symlinks; all observed model regular files have nlink=1.
ODISE has an external symlink to /root/.cache/sd_checkpoints/v1-5-pruned-emaonly.ckpt. Preserve its target string and audit resolution before cutover; do not follow it during copying.
Keep ~/.cache/huggingface token/config and non-model caches untouched; do not move the entire .cache directory.
Validate files/byte counts, revisions and snapshot links plus offline config/tokenizer/model-path resolution before removing old bytes.
Account for NFS latency/availability and shared cache concurrency; other root projects use the same default model paths.
Keep a rollback path through cutover; source cleanup must occur only after validation and explicit approval.

conservative_buffer.note: A five-GB growth buffer is recommended. The current restricted audit cannot certify that unmeasured .codex fits this budget; do not declare the 50GB target achieved. Environment splitting is not inherently required if model relocation and total accounting fit, but no environment removal is authorized or recommended.

conclusion: Ordinary cache cleanup alone cannot reach 50 GB. Preserving current methods requires keeping model weights or relocating them. With batch A plus 44.579 GB of model migration, the audited remainder is 43.666 GB plus the unknown excluded .codex allocation. Therefore 50 GB is conditionally feasible without tearing down environments, but cannot be certified from this restricted audit. If migration is disallowed and model/runtime functionality must remain intact, no safe <=50 GB plan is established.
